recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片見多個大型異常淋巴細胞：核大而圓、染色質細緻，細胞質強嗜鹼性且有小空泡，部分拉出細長尾巴（手鏡狀），與周圍小型造血細胞對比明顯，符合血管內大型 B 細胞淋巴瘤細胞。
features: Large atypical lymphoid cells, several times the size of red cells
Round to oval nuclei with finely granular/vesicular chromatin and inconspicuous to small nucleoli
Moderate, deeply basophilic cytoplasm with small vacuoles
Cytoplasmic tails and blebs producing hand-mirror shapes
Admixed normal marrow elements (neutrophil, myelocytes, erythroid precursors)
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows numerous large atypical lymphoid cells with round to oval nuclei, finely dispersed chromatin, and moderate amounts of deeply basophilic, finely vacuolated cytoplasm, some with cytoplasmic tails and blebs. These cells are markedly larger than the admixed normal granulocytic and erythroid precursors. Findings are consistent with involvement by a large B-cell lymphoma; in the clinical context, intravascular large B-cell lymphoma is favored, and correlation with biopsy (intrasinusoidal CD20+ cells) and flow cytometry is recommended.

ddx.vs: Monoblasts have folded nuclei, gray-blue cytoplasm with fine granules, and are MPO/NSE and CD33/CD64 positive rather than CD19/CD20 positive.
Plasmablasts show eccentric nuclei with perinuclear hof and prominent central nucleoli and are CD138+ and CD20-negative.
Burkitt cells are medium-sized with multiple lipid vacuoles in deeply basophilic cytoplasm, very high proliferation, and MYC rearrangement.
Metastatic tumor cells form cohesive clumps and are CD45-negative with lineage-specific markers.
